## Eliminate repeated regex compilation during XML tag renaming

When loading legacy OpenSim model files, the XML tag renaming logic constructs new regular expression objects for every element examined. Profiling shows this repeated regex compilation consumes significant time (about 5% of runtime) when loading many model files. The goal is to ensure these pattern objects are created only once per application execution, rather than being rebuilt for each element during file loading.

465: // REGISTER TYPE
466: //-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
467: 
468: //_____________________________________________________________________________
469: /*
470:  * Register a supported object type.  A global list of all supported objects
471:  * (i.e., objects derived from Object) is kept mainly for two purposes:
472:  *
473:  * ---- Object Deserialization ----
474:  * Once a type T is registered, that type can be read from XML files
475:  * assuming that the type has implemented the following methods:
476:  *  1)  copy constructor
477:  *  2)  virtual T* clone() const
478:  *  3)  static const char* getClassName()
479:  *  4)  T& operator=() 
480:  *
481:  * ---- Initialization by Default Object ----
482:  * When objects are deserialized, they are constructed based on the registered
483:  * type and receive all of the registered type's property values.  These
484:  * values are over-ridden only if there is an element within an XML file that
485:  * overrides a default element.
486:  *
487:  * Because this method is static, registration of object types needs to be
488:  * done only once per process and an object does not need to be
489:  * instantiated to do so.
490:  *
491:  * This method makes a copy of the specified object.
492:  *
493:  * @param aObject Object of the type to be registered.  If the type is
494:  * already registered, the current object is replaced by a copy of
495:  * the specified object.
496:  * @see isValidDefault()
497:  */
498: /*static*/ void Object::
499: registerType(const Object& aObject)
500: {
501:     // GET TYPE
502:     const string& type = aObject.getConcreteClassName();
503:     if(type.empty()) {
504:         log_error("Object.registerType: no type name has been set.");
505:         return;
506:     }
507:     log_debug("Object.registerType: {}.", type);
508: 
509:     // REPLACE IF A MATCHING TYPE IS ALREADY REGISTERED
510:     for(int i=0; i <_registeredTypes.size(); ++i) {
511:         Object *object = _registeredTypes.get(i);
512:         if(object->getConcreteClassName() == type) {
513:             log_debug("Object.registerType: replacing registered object of "
514:                       "type {} with a new default object of the same type.",
515:                       type);
516:             Object* defaultObj = aObject.clone();
517:             defaultObj->setName(DEFAULT_NAME);
518:             _registeredTypes.set(i,defaultObj);
519:             _mapTypesToDefaultObjects[type]= defaultObj;
520:             return;
521:         } 
522:     }
523: 
524:     // REGISTERING FOR THE FIRST TIME -- APPEND
525:     Object* defaultObj = aObject.clone();
526:     defaultObj->setName(DEFAULT_NAME);
527:     _registeredTypes.append(defaultObj);
528:     _mapTypesToDefaultObjects[type]= defaultObj;
529: }
530: 
531: /*static*/ void Object::
532: renameType(const std::string& oldTypeName, const std::string& newTypeName)
533: {
534:     if(oldTypeName == newTypeName)
535:         return; 
536: 
537:     std::map<std::string,Object*>::const_iterator p = 
538:         _mapTypesToDefaultObjects.find(newTypeName);
539: 
540:     if (p == _mapTypesToDefaultObjects.end())
541:         throw OpenSim::Exception(
542:             "Object::renameType(): illegal attempt to rename object type "
543:             + oldTypeName + " to " + newTypeName + " which is unregistered.",
544:             __FILE__, __LINE__);
545: 
546:     _renamedTypesMap[oldTypeName] = newTypeName;
547: }
548: 
549: /*static*/ const Object* Object::
550: getDefaultInstanceOfType(const std::string& objectTypeTag) {
551:     std::string actualName = objectTypeTag;
552:     bool wasRenamed = false; // for a better error message
553: 
554:     // First apply renames if any.
555: 
556:     // Avoid an infinite loop if there is a cycle in the rename table.
557:     const int MaxRenames = (int)_renamedTypesMap.size();
558:     int renameCount = 0;
559:     while(true) {
560:         std::map<std::string,std::string>::const_iterator newNamep =
561:             _renamedTypesMap.find(actualName);
562:         if (newNamep == _renamedTypesMap.end())
563:             break; // actualName has not been renamed
564: 
565:         if (++renameCount > MaxRenames) {
566:             throw OpenSim::Exception(
567:                 "Object::getDefaultInstanceOfType(): cycle in rename table "
568:                 "found when looking for '" + objectTypeTag + "'.");
569:         }
570: 
571:         actualName = newNamep->second;
572:         wasRenamed = true;
573:     }
574: 
575:     // Look up the "actualName" default object and return it.
576:     std::map<std::string,Object*>::const_iterator p = 
577:         _mapTypesToDefaultObjects.find(actualName);
578:     if (p != _mapTypesToDefaultObjects.end())
579:         return p->second;
580: 
581:     // The requested object was not registered. That's OK normally but is
582:     // a bug if we went through the rename table since you are only allowed
583:     // to rename things to registered objects.
584:     if (wasRenamed) {
585:         throw OpenSim::Exception(
586:             "Object::getDefaultInstanceOfType(): '" + objectTypeTag
587:             + "' was renamed to '" + actualName 
588:             + "' which is not the name of a registered object.");
589:     }
590: 
591:     return NULL;
592: }
593: 
594: /*
595:  * Create a new instance of the type indicated by objectTypeTag.
596:  * The instance is initialized to the default Object of corresponding type.
597:  * Note that renaming of old types may occur; the returned object will have
598:  * the current type tag.
599:  */
600: /*static*/ Object* Object::
601: newInstanceOfType(const std::string& objectTypeTag)
602: {
603:     const Object* defaultObj = getDefaultInstanceOfType(objectTypeTag);
604:     if (defaultObj)
605:         return defaultObj->clone();
606:     log_error("Object::newInstanceOfType(): object type '{}' is not a registered "
607:             "Object! It will be ignored.",
608:             objectTypeTag);
609:     throw Exception("Object::newInstanceOfType(): object type '{" +
610:                     objectTypeTag
611:                     +"}' is not a registered Object! It will be ignored.");
612: 
613:     return NULL;
614: }

616: /*
617:  * getRegisteredTypenames() is a utility to retrieve all the typenames 
618:  * registered so far. This is done by traversing the registered objects map, 
619:  * so only concrete classes are dealt with. The result returned in rTypeNames 
620:  * should not be cached while more dlls are loaded as they get stale
621:  * instead the list should be constructed whenever in doubt.
622:  */
623: /*static*/ void Object::
624: getRegisteredTypenames(Array<std::string>& rTypeNames)
625: {
626:     std::map<string,Object*>::const_iterator p = 
627:         _mapTypesToDefaultObjects.begin();
628:     for (; p != _mapTypesToDefaultObjects.end(); ++p)
629:         rTypeNames.append(p->first);
630:     // Renamed type names don't appear in the registeredTypes map, unless
631:     // they were separately registered.
632: }

640: template<class T> static void 
641: UpdateFromXMLNodeSimpleProperty(Property_Deprecated* aProperty, 
642:                                 SimTK::Xml::Element& aNode, 
643:                                 const string&        aName)
644: {
645:     aProperty->setValueIsDefault(true);
646: 
647:     SimTK::Xml::element_iterator iter = aNode.element_begin(aName);
648:     if (iter == aNode.element_end()) return;    // Not found
649: 
650:     T value;
651:     iter->getValueAs(value); // fails for Nan, infinity, -infinity, true/false
652:     aProperty->setValue(value);
653:     aProperty->setValueIsDefault(false);
654: }

656: template<class T> static void 
657: UpdateFromXMLNodeArrayProperty(Property_Deprecated* aProperty, 
658:                                SimTK::Xml::Element& aNode, 
659:                                const string&        aName)
660: {
661:     aProperty->setValueIsDefault(true);
662: 
663:     SimTK::Xml::element_iterator iter = aNode.element_begin(aName);
664:     if (iter == aNode.element_end()) return;    // Not found
665: 
666:     SimTK::Array_<T> value;
667:     iter->getValueAs(value);
668: 
669:     OpenSim::Array<T> osimValue;
670:     osimValue.setSize(value.size());
671:     for(unsigned i=0; i< value.size(); i++) osimValue[i]=value[i];
672:     aProperty->setValue(osimValue);
673:     aProperty->setValueIsDefault(false);
674: }

679: // Populate this Object from XML element corresponding to an Object Property.
680: // We check for a file="xxx" attribute and read the object from that file
681: // if it is present. Otherwise we punt to updateFromXMLNode() and read the
682: // object directly from the supplied element.
683: void Object::readObjectFromXMLNodeOrFile
684:    (SimTK::Xml::Element& objectElement, 
685:     int                  versionNumber)
686: {
687:     // If object is from non-inlined, detect it and set attributes
688:     // However we need to do that on the finalized object as copying
689:     // does not keep track of XML related issues
690:     const std::string file = 
691:         objectElement.getOptionalAttributeValueAs<std::string>("file", "");
692: 
693:     // otherwise object is described in file and it has root element
694:     const bool inlinedObject = (file == ""); 
695: 
696:     if (inlinedObject) {
697:         // This object comes from the main XML document.
698:         updateFromXMLNode(objectElement, versionNumber);
699:         return;
700:     }
701: 
702:     // This object specifies an external file from which it should be read.
703: 
704:     // When including contents from another file it's assumed file path is 
705:     // relative to the current working directory, which is usually set to be
706:     // the directory that contained the top-level XML file.
707:     XMLDocument* newDoc=0;
708:     try {
709:         log_info("Reading object from file [{}] cwd ={}.",
710:                 file, IO::getCwd());
711:          newDoc = new XMLDocument(file);
712:         _document = newDoc;
713:     } catch(const std::exception& ex){
714:         log_error("Failure reading object from file [{}] cwd ={} Error:{}",
715:                 file, IO::getCwd(), ex.what());
716:         return;
717:     }
718:     _inlined=false;
719:     SimTK::Xml::Element e = newDoc->getRootDataElement();
720:     updateFromXMLNode(e, newDoc->getDocumentVersion());
721: }

779: //-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
780: // UPDATE OBJECT
781: //-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
782: void Object::updateFromXMLNode(SimTK::Xml::Element& aNode, int versionNumber)
783: {
784: try {
785:     // NAME
786:     const string dName = 
787:         aNode.getOptionalAttributeValueAs<std::string>("name", "");
788: 
789:     // Set the name of this object.
790:     setName(dName);
791: 
792:     // UPDATE DEFAULT OBJECTS
793:     updateDefaultObjectsFromXMLNode(); // May need to pass in aNode
794: 
795:     // LOOP THROUGH PROPERTIES
796:     for(int i=0; i < _propertyTable.getNumProperties(); ++i) {
797:         AbstractProperty& prop = _propertyTable.updAbstractPropertyByIndex(i);
798:         prop.readFromXMLParentElement(aNode, versionNumber);
799:     }
800: 
801:     // LOOP THROUGH DEPRECATED PROPERTIES
802:     // TODO: get rid of this
803:     for(int i=0;i<_propertySet.getSize();i++) {
804: 
805:         Property_Deprecated* property = _propertySet.get(i);
806: 
807:         // TYPE
808:         Property_Deprecated::PropertyType type = property->getType();   
809: 
810:         // NAME
811:         string name = property->getName();
812:         SimTK::String valueString;
813:         SimTK::String lowerCaseValueString;
814:         SimTK::Xml::element_iterator iter;
815:         SimTK::Array_<SimTK::String> value;
816:         OpenSim::Array<bool> osimValue;
817:         // VALUE
818:         switch(type) {
819: 
820:         // Bool
821:         case(Property_Deprecated::Bool) : 
822:             property->setValueIsDefault(true);
823:             iter= aNode.element_begin(name);
824:             if (iter == aNode.element_end()) break; // Not found
825:             iter->getValueAs(valueString); // true/false
826:             lowerCaseValueString = valueString.toLower();
827:             property->setValue(lowerCaseValueString=="true"?true:false);
828:             //UpdateFromXMLNodeSimpleProperty<bool>(property, aNode, name);
829:             property->setValueIsDefault(false);
830:             break;
831:         // Int
832:         case(Property_Deprecated::Int) :
833:             UpdateFromXMLNodeSimpleProperty<int>(property, aNode, name);
834:             break;
835:         // Double
836:         case(Property_Deprecated::Dbl) :
837:             property->setValueIsDefault(true);
838:             iter= aNode.element_begin(name);
839:             if (iter == aNode.element_end()) continue;  // Not found
840:             iter->getValueAs(valueString); // special values
841:             lowerCaseValueString = valueString.toLower();
842:             if (lowerCaseValueString=="infinity" || lowerCaseValueString=="inf")
843:                 property->setValue(SimTK::Infinity);
844:             else if (lowerCaseValueString=="-infinity" || lowerCaseValueString=="-inf")
845:                 property->setValue(-SimTK::Infinity);
846:             else if (lowerCaseValueString=="nan")
847:                 property->setValue(SimTK::NaN);
848:             else
849:                 UpdateFromXMLNodeSimpleProperty<double>(property, aNode, name);
850:             property->setValueIsDefault(false);
851:             break;
852:         // Str
853:         case(Property_Deprecated::Str) : 
854:             UpdateFromXMLNodeSimpleProperty<string>(property, aNode, name);
855:             break;
856:         // BoolArray
857:         case(Property_Deprecated::BoolArray) : 
858:             // Parse as a String array then map true/false to boolean values
859:             property->setValueIsDefault(true);
860:             iter = aNode.element_begin(name);
861:             if (iter == aNode.element_end()) continue;  // Not found
862:             iter->getValueAs(value);
863:             //cout << value << endl;
864:             osimValue.setSize(value.size());
865:             for(unsigned i=0; i< value.size(); i++) osimValue[i]=(value[i]=="true");
866:             property->setValue(osimValue);
867:             property->setValueIsDefault(false);
868:             break;
869:         // IntArray
870:         case(Property_Deprecated::IntArray) :
871:             UpdateFromXMLNodeArrayProperty<int>(property,aNode,name);
872:             break;
873:         // DblArray
874:         case(Property_Deprecated::DblArray) :
875:         case(Property_Deprecated::DblVec) :
876:         case(Property_Deprecated::Transform) :
877:             UpdateFromXMLNodeArrayProperty<double>(property,aNode,name);
878:             break;
879:         // StrArray
880:         case(Property_Deprecated::StrArray) :
881:             UpdateFromXMLNodeArrayProperty<string>(property,aNode,name);
882:             break;
883: 
884:         // Obj
885:         case(Property_Deprecated::Obj) : {
886:             property->setValueIsDefault(true);
887:             Object &object = property->getValueObj();
888:             SimTK::Xml::element_iterator iter = 
889:                 aNode.element_begin(object.getConcreteClassName());
890:             if (iter == aNode.element_end()) 
891:                 continue;   // No element of this object type found.
892: 
893:             // If matchName is set, search through elements of this type to find
894:             // one that has a "name" attribute that matches the name of this
895:             // object.
896:             if (property->getMatchName()) {
897:                 while(object.getName() != 
898:                         iter->getOptionalAttributeValueAs<std::string>("name", dName) 
899:                       && iter != aNode.element_end()) 
900:                 {
901:                     ++iter;
902:                 }
903:                 if (iter != aNode.element_end()) {
904:                     object.readObjectFromXMLNodeOrFile(*iter, versionNumber);
905:                     property->setValueIsDefault(false);
906:                 }
907:             } else {
908:                 object.readObjectFromXMLNodeOrFile(*iter, versionNumber);
909:                 property->setValueIsDefault(false);
910:             }
911:             break; 
912:         }
913: 
914:         // ObjArray AND ObjPtr (handled very similarly)
915:         case(Property_Deprecated::ObjArray) : 
916:         case(Property_Deprecated::ObjPtr) : {
917:             property->setValueIsDefault(true);
918: 
919:             // FIND THE PROPERTY ELEMENT (in aNode)
920:             const SimTK::Xml::element_iterator propElementIter = aNode.element_begin(name);
921:             if (propElementIter==aNode.element_end()) 
922:                 break;
923: 
924:             if(type==Property_Deprecated::ObjArray) {
925:                 // CLEAR EXISTING OBJECT ARRAY
926:                 // Eran: Moved after elmt check above so that values set by constructor are kept if
927:                 // property is not specified in the xml file
928:                 property->clearObjArray();
929:             }
930: 
931:             property->setValueIsDefault(false);
932: 
933:             // LOOP THROUGH PROPERTY ELEMENT'S CHILD ELEMENTS
934:             // Each element is expected to be an Object of some type given
935:             // by the element's tag.
936:             Object *object =NULL;
937:             int objectsFound = 0;
938:             SimTK::Xml::element_iterator iter = propElementIter->element_begin();
939:             while(iter != propElementIter->element_end()){
940:                 // Create an Object of the element tag's type.
941:                 object = newInstanceOfType(iter->getElementTag());
942:                 objectsFound++;
943: 
944:                 if(type==Property_Deprecated::ObjPtr) {
945:                     if(objectsFound > 1){
946:                         //throw XMLParsingException("Found multiple objects under "+name+" tag, but expected only one.",objElmt,__FILE__,__LINE__);
947:                     }
948:                     else{
949:                         property->setValue(object);
950:                     }
951:                 } else {
952:                     property->appendValue(object);
953:                 }
954:                 object->updateFromXMLNode(*iter, versionNumber);
955:                 iter++;
956:             }
957:                 
958:             break; }
959: 
960:         // NOT RECOGNIZED
961:         default :
962:             cout<<"Object.UpdateObject: WARN- unrecognized property type."<<endl;
963:             break;
964:         }
965:     }
966: 
967: 
968:     } catch (const Exception &ex) {
969:         // Important to catch exceptions here so we can restore current working directory...
970:         // And then we can re-throw the exception
971:         throw(ex);
972:     }
973: 
974: }

977: // UPDATE DEFAULT OBJECTS FROM XML NODE
978: //-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
979: //_____________________________________________________________________________
980: /**
981:  * Update the registered default objects based on an object's XML node.
982:  *
983:  * This method looks for an element with a tag name "defaults" and reads
984:  * the objects in that element and registers them using the method
985:  * Object::registerType().
986:  */
987: void Object::
988: updateDefaultObjectsFromXMLNode()
989: {

68:         if (normalizedPath.empty()) {

74:             ++it;

80:     /**
81:      * Returns a normalized form of `path`. A normalized path string is
82:      * guaranteed to:
83:      *
84:      * - Not contain any *internal* or *trailing* relative elements (e.g.
85:      *   'a/../b').
86:      *
87:      *     - It may *start* with relative elements (e.g. '../a/b'), but only
88:      *       if the path is non-absolute (e.g. "/../a/b" is invalid)
89:      *
90:      * - Not contain any invalid characters (e.g. '\\', '*')
91:      *
92:      * - Not contain any repeated separators (e.g. 'a///b' --> 'a/b')
93:      *
94:      * Any attempt to step above the root of the expression with '..' will
95:      * result in an exception being thrown (e.g. "a/../.." will throw).
96:      *
97:      * This method is useful for path traversal and path manipulation
98:      * methods, because the above ensures that (e.g.) paths can be
99:      * concatenated and split into individual elements using basic
100:      * string manipulation techniques.
101:      */
102:     std::string normalize(std::string path) {
103:         // note: this implementation is fairly low-level and involves mutating
104:         //       `path` quite a bit. The test suite is heavily relied on for
105:         //       developing this kind of tricky code.
106:         //
107:         //       the reason it's done this way is because profiling shown that
108:         //       `ComponentPath` was accounting for ~6-10 % of OpenSim's CPU
109:         //       usage for component-heavy sims. The reason this was so high
110:         //       was because `ComponentPath` used a simpler algorithm that
111:         //       split the path into a std::vector.
112:         //
113:         //       usually, that alg. wouldn't be a problem, but path
114:         //       normalization can happen millions of times during a simulation,
115:         //       all those vector allocations can thrash the allocator and
116:         //       increase L1 misses.
117: 
118:         // assert that `path` contains no invalid chars
119:         if (path.find_first_of(newInvalidChars) != std::string::npos) {
120:             OPENSIM_THROW(OpenSim::Exception, path + ": The supplied path contains invalid characters.");
121:         }
122: 
123:         // pathEnd is guaranteed to be a NUL terminator since C++11
124:         char* pathBegin = &path[0];
125:         char* pathEnd = &path[path.size()];
126: 
127:         // helper: shift n chars starting at newStart+n such that, after,
128:         // newStart..end is equal to what newStart+n..end was before.
129:         auto shift = [&](char* newStart, size_t n) {
130:             std::copy(newStart + n, pathEnd, newStart);
131:             pathEnd -= n;
132:         };
133: 
134:         // helper: grab 3 lookahead chars, using NUL as a senteniel to
135:         // indicate "past the end of the content".
136:         //
137:         // - The maximum lookahead is 3 characters because the parsing
138:         //   code below needs to be able to detect the upcoming input 
139:         //   pattern "..[/\0]"
140:         struct Lookahead { char a, b, c; };
141:         auto getLookahead = [](char* start, char* end) {
142:             return Lookahead{
143:                 start < end - 0 ? start[0] : nul,
144:                 start < end - 1 ? start[1] : nul,
145:                 start < end - 2 ? start[2] : nul,
146:             };
147:         };
148: 
149: 
150:         // remove duplicate adjacent separators
151:         for (char* c = pathBegin; c != pathEnd; ++c) {
152:             Lookahead l = getLookahead(c, pathEnd);
153:             if (l.a == separator && l.b == separator) {
154:                 shift(c--, 1);
155:             }
156:         }
157: 
158:         bool isAbsolute = *pathBegin == separator;
159:         char* cursor = isAbsolute ? pathBegin + 1 : pathBegin;
160: 
161:         // skip/dereference relative elements *at the start of a path*
162:         Lookahead l = getLookahead(cursor, pathEnd);
163:         while (l.a == '.') {
164:             switch (l.b) {
165:             case separator:
166:                 shift(cursor, 2);
167:                 break;
168:             case nul:
169:                 shift(cursor, 1);
170:                 break;
171:             case '.': {
172:                 if (l.c == separator || l.c == nul) {
173:                     // starts with '..' element: only allowed if the path
174:                     // is relative
175:                     if (isAbsolute) {
176:                         OPENSIM_THROW(OpenSim::Exception, path + ": is an invalid path: it is absolute, but starts with relative elements.");
177:                     }
178: 
179:                     // if not absolute, then make sure `contentStart` skips
180:                     // past these elements because the alg can't reduce
181:                     // them down
182:                     if (l.c == separator) {
183:                         cursor += 3;
184:                     } else {
185:                         cursor += 2;
186:                     }
187:                 } else {
188:                     // normal element that starts with '..'
189:                     ++cursor;
190:                 }
191:                 break;
192:             }
193:             default:
194:                 // normal element that starts with '.'
195:                 ++cursor;
196:                 break;
197:             }
198: 
199:             l = getLookahead(cursor, pathEnd);
200:         }
201: 
202:         char* contentStart = cursor;
203: 
204:         // invariants:
205:         //
206:         // - the root path element (if any) has been skipped
207:         // - `contentStart` points to the start of the non-relative content of
208:         //   the supplied path string
209:         // - `path` contains no duplicate adjacent separators
210:         // - `[0..offset]` is normalized path string, but may contain a
211:         //   trailing slash
212:         // - `[contentStart..offset] is the normalized *content* of the path
213:         //   string
214: 
215:         while (cursor < pathEnd) {
216:             Lookahead l = getLookahead(cursor, pathEnd);
217: 
218:             if (l.a == '.' && (l.b == nul || l.b == separator)) {
219:                 // handle '.' (if found)
220:                 size_t charsInCurEl = l.b == separator ? 2 : 1;
221:                 shift(cursor, charsInCurEl);
222: 
223:             } else if (l.a == '.' && l.b == '.' && (l.c == nul || l.c == separator)) {
224:                 // handle '..' (if found)
225: 
226:                 if (cursor == contentStart) {
227:                     OPENSIM_THROW(OpenSim::Exception, path + ": cannot handle '..' element in a path string: dereferencing this would hop above the root of the path.");
228:                 }
229: 
230:                 // search backwards for previous separator
231:                 char* prevSeparator = cursor - 2;
232:                 while (prevSeparator > contentStart && *prevSeparator != separator) {
233:                     --prevSeparator;
234:                 }
235: 
236:                 char* prevStart = prevSeparator <= contentStart ? contentStart : prevSeparator + 1;
237:                 size_t charsInCurEl = (l.c == separator) ? 3 : 2;
238:                 size_t charsInPrevEl = cursor - prevStart;
239: 
240:                 cursor = prevStart;
241:                 shift(cursor, charsInPrevEl + charsInCurEl);
242: 
243:             } else {
244:                 // non-relative element: skip past the next separator or end
245:                 cursor = std::find(cursor, pathEnd, separator) + 1;
246:             }
247:         }
248: 
249:         // edge case:
250:         // - There was a trailing slash in the input and, post reduction, the output
251:         //   string is only a slash. However, the input path wasnt initially an
252:         //   absolute path, so the output should be "", not "/"
253:         {
254:             char* beg = isAbsolute ? pathBegin + 1 : pathBegin;
255:             if (pathEnd - beg > 0 && pathEnd[-1] == separator) {
256:                 --pathEnd;
257:             }
258:         }
259: 
260:         // resize output to only contain the normalized range
261:         path.resize(pathEnd - pathBegin);
262: 
263:         return path;
264:     }

306: ComponentPath ComponentPath::formRelativePath(const ComponentPath& otherPath) const {
307:     // helper: returns a path string containing `n` step ups (e.g. "../../")
308:     static auto generateStepUps = [](size_t n) {
309:         std::string rv;
310:         for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
311:             rv += "..";
312:             rv += separator;
313:         }
314:         return rv;
315:     };
316: 
317:     if (!isAbsolute()) {
318:         OPENSIM_THROW(Exception, _path + ": is not an absolute path.");
319:     }
320: 
321:     if (!otherPath.isAbsolute()) {
322:         OPENSIM_THROW(Exception, _path + ": is not an absolute path.");
323:     }
324: 
325:     // readability: the resulting path goes FROM p1 and TO p2
326:     const std::string& p1 = otherPath._path;
327:     const std::string& p2 = this->_path;
328: 
329:     // compute the lexographic mismatch between p1 and p2
330:     const size_t mismatch = [&]() {
331:         auto shortest = static_cast<std::string::difference_type>(std::min(p1.size(), p2.size()));
332:         auto p = std::mismatch(p1.begin(), p1.begin() + shortest, p2.begin());
333:         return static_cast<size_t>(std::distance(p1.begin(), p.first));
334:     }();
335: 
336:     // handle edge cases: see test suite for example inputs
337:     ComponentPath rv;
338: 
339:     if (p1[mismatch] == nul && p2[mismatch] == nul) {
340:         // p1 == p2
341:         rv = ComponentPath{""};
342:     } else if (p1.size() == 1 && p1[0] == separator) {
343:         // p1 is just "/", p2 is defined to be a direct subpath beginning after
344:         // the "/"
345:         rv = ComponentPath{p2.substr(1)};
346:     } else if (p1[mismatch] == nul && p2[mismatch] == separator) {
347:         // p2 is a direct subpath of p1, so only step down
348:         rv = ComponentPath{p2.substr(mismatch + 1)};
349:     } else if (p1[mismatch] == separator && p2[mismatch] == nul) {
350:         // p1 is a direct subpath of p2, so only step up
351:         size_t stepUps = std::count(p1.begin() + mismatch, p1.end(), separator);
352:         rv = ComponentPath{generateStepUps(stepUps)};
353:     } else {
354:         // There is a divergence between the two paths. Step up to the
355:         // divergence point (dir) then step down to the target
356:         size_t divergencePoint = p1.rfind(separator, mismatch - 1);
357: 
358:         // step up in p1 and then step down in p2
359:         size_t stepUps = std::count(p1.begin() + divergencePoint, p1.end(), separator);
360:         std::string path = generateStepUps(stepUps);
361:         path += p2.substr(divergencePoint + 1);
362: 
363:         rv = ComponentPath{std::move(path)};
364:     }
365: 
366:     return rv;
367: }

89:     cmake_parse_arguments(
90:         OSIMRP "${options}" "${oneValueArgs}" "${multiValueArgs}" ${ARGN})
91:     if(OSIMRP_ABSOLUTE AND (OSIMRP_FROM OR OSIMRP_EXECUTABLE OR OSIMRP_LOADER))
92:         message(AUTHOR_WARNING
93:             "Cannot specify both ABSOLUTE and FROM, EXECUTABLE, or LOADER.")
94:     endif()
95: 
96:     if(NOT OPENSIM_USE_INSTALL_RPATH OR NOT OPENSIM_COPY_DEPENDENCIES
97:             OR OPENSIM_INSTALL_UNIX_FHS)
98:         return()
99:     endif()

101:     file(RELATIVE_PATH simbody_root_to_simbody_lib_dir 
102:         "${Simbody_ROOT_DIR}" "${Simbody_LIB_DIR}")
103:     set(root_to_simbody_lib_dir
104:         "${OPENSIM_INSTALL_SIMBODYDIR}/${simbody_root_to_simbody_lib_dir}")
105: 
106:     if(OSIMRP_ABSOLUTE)
107:         set_property(TARGET ${OSIMRP_TARGET} APPEND PROPERTY INSTALL_RPATH

115:                 FROM ${OSIMRP_FROM} TO ${root_to_simbody_lib_dir})

141: # Create an OpenSim API library. Here are the arguments:
142: # VENDORLIB: If this is a vendor library, specify "VENDORLIB" as the first
143: #   argument. Otherwise, omit.
144: # LOWERINCLUDEDIRNAME: When installing the headers for this library, make the
145: #   name of the library all lower-case (e.g., Lepton -> lepton).
146: # EXCLUDEFROMPYTHON: Do not install this library into the python package.
147: # KIT: Name of the library (e.g., Common).
148: # AUTHORS: A string listing authors of the library.
149: # LINKLIBS: List of libraries (targets) to link against.
150: # INCLUDES: List of header files for the library (obtain via file(GLOB ...)).
151: # SOURCES: List of cpp files for the library (obtain via file(GLOB ...)).
152: # TESTDIRS: List of subdirectories that contain tests (and a CMakeLists.txt).
153: # INCLUDEDIRS (optional): Affects how header files are installed. Use this if
154: #   the library directory contains subdirectories with header files. If this is
155: #   the case, this variable should be a list of those subdirectories (relative
156: #   paths). See OpenSim/Simulation/CMakeLists.txt for an example. If omitted,
157: #   all the headers specified under INCLUDES are installed into the same
158: #   directory in the installation tree.
159: # INCLUDEINSTALLREL (optional): If INCLUDEDIRS is specified, remove
160: #   "INCLUDEINSTALLREL" from the location of the installed headers.
161: #
162: # Here's an example from OpenSim/Common/CMakeLists.txt:
163: #
164: #   OpenSimAddLibrary(
165: #       KIT Common
166: #       AUTHORS "Clay_Anderson-Ayman_Habib_and_Peter_Loan"
167: #       LINKLIBS ${Simbody_LIBRARIES}
168: #       INCLUDES ${INCLUDES}
169: #       SOURCES ${SOURCES}
170: #       TESTDIRS "Test"
171: #       )
172: function(OpenSimAddLibrary)
173: 
174:     # Parse arguments.
175:     # ----------------
176:     # http://www.cmake.org/cmake/help/v2.8.9/cmake.html#module:CMakeParseArguments
177:     set(options VENDORLIB LOWERINCLUDEDIRNAME EXCLUDEFROMPYTHON)
178:     set(oneValueArgs KIT AUTHORS INCLUDEINSTALLREL)
179:     set(multiValueArgs LINKLIBS INCLUDES SOURCES TESTDIRS INCLUDEDIRS)
180:     cmake_parse_arguments(
181:         OSIMADDLIB "${options}" "${oneValueArgs}" "${multiValueArgs}" ${ARGN})
182: 
183:     string(TOUPPER "${OSIMADDLIB_KIT}" OSIMADDLIB_UKIT)
184: 
185: 
186:     # Version stuff.
187:     # --------------
188:     set(OSIMADDLIB_LIBRARY_NAME osim${OSIMADDLIB_KIT})
189: 
190:     add_definitions(
191:         -DOPENSIM_${OSIMADDLIB_UKIT}_LIBRARY_NAME=${OSIMADDLIB_LIBRARY_NAME}
192:         -DOPENSIM_${OSIMADDLIB_UKIT}_MAJOR_VERSION=${OPENSIM_MAJOR_VERSION}
193:         -DOPENSIM_${OSIMADDLIB_UKIT}_MINOR_VERSION=${OPENSIM_MINOR_VERSION}
194:         -DOPENSIM_${OSIMADDLIB_UKIT}_BUILD_VERSION=${OPENSIM_PATCH_VERSION}
195:         -DOPENSIM_${OSIMADDLIB_UKIT}_COPYRIGHT_YEARS="2005-2017"
196:         -DOPENSIM_${OSIMADDLIB_UKIT}_AUTHORS="${AUTHORS}"
197:         -DOPENSIM_${OSIMADDLIB_UKIT}_TYPE="Shared"
198:         )
199: 
200: 
201:     # Add the library.
202:     # ----------------
203:     # These next few lines are the most important:
204: 
205:     # Create the library using the provided source and include files.
206:     add_library(${OSIMADDLIB_LIBRARY_NAME} SHARED
207:         ${OSIMADDLIB_SOURCES} ${OSIMADDLIB_INCLUDES})
208: 
209:     target_include_directories(${OSIMADDLIB_LIBRARY_NAME} 
210:         # Used when building this target:
211:         PRIVATE "${OpenSim_SOURCE_DIR}"
212:                 "${OpenSim_SOURCE_DIR}/Vendors/lepton/include"
213:         # Used by other targets in this project:
214:         INTERFACE $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${OpenSim_SOURCE_DIR}>
215:                   $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${OpenSim_SOURCE_DIR}/Vendors/lepton/include>
216:         # Used by client projects using an installed OpenSim:
217:         INTERFACE $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}>
218:                   $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}/OpenSim>
219:         )
220: 
221:     # This target links to the libraries provided as arguments to this func.
222:     target_link_libraries(${OSIMADDLIB_LIBRARY_NAME} ${OSIMADDLIB_LINKLIBS})
223: 
224:     # This is for exporting classes on Windows.
225:     if(OSIMADDLIB_VENDORLIB)
226:         set(OSIMADDLIB_FOLDER "Vendor Libraries")
227:     else()
228:         set(OSIMADDLIB_FOLDER "Libraries")
229:     endif()
230:     set_target_properties(${OSIMADDLIB_LIBRARY_NAME} PROPERTIES
231:        DEFINE_SYMBOL OSIM${OSIMADDLIB_UKIT}_EXPORTS
232:        FOLDER "${OSIMADDLIB_FOLDER}" # For Visual Studio.
233:     )
234: 
235:     # Install.
236:     # --------
237:     # Shared libraries are needed at runtime for applications, so we put them
238:     # at the top level in OpenSim/bin/*.dll (Windows) or OpenSim/lib/*.so
239:     # (Linux) or OpemSim/lib/*.dylib (Mac). Windows .lib files, and Linux/Mac
240:     # .a static archives are only needed at link time so go in sdk/lib.
241:     if(WIN32)
242:         set(OSIMADDLIB_LIBRARY_DESTINATION sdk/lib)
243:     else()
244:         set(OSIMADDLIB_LIBRARY_DESTINATION lib)
245:     endif()
246:     install(TARGETS ${OSIMADDLIB_LIBRARY_NAME}
247:         EXPORT OpenSimTargets
248:         RUNTIME DESTINATION "${CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR}"
249:         LIBRARY DESTINATION "${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}"
250:         ARCHIVE DESTINATION "${OPENSIM_INSTALL_ARCHIVEDIR}")
251:     if(BUILD_PYTHON_WRAPPING AND OPENSIM_PYTHON_STANDALONE
252:             AND NOT OSIMADDLIB_EXCLUDEFROMPYTHON)
253:         if (WIN32)
254:             install(TARGETS ${OSIMADDLIB_LIBRARY_NAME}
255:                 RUNTIME DESTINATION "${OPENSIM_INSTALL_PYTHONDIR}/opensim")
256:         else()
257:             install(TARGETS ${OSIMADDLIB_LIBRARY_NAME}
258:                 LIBRARY DESTINATION "${OPENSIM_INSTALL_PYTHONDIR}/opensim")
259:         endif()
260:     endif()
261: 
262:     # Install headers.
263:     # ----------------
264:     set(_INCLUDE_PREFIX "${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}/OpenSim")
265:     if(OSIMADDLIB_LOWERINCLUDEDIRNAME)
266:         string(TOLOWER "${OSIMADDLIB_KIT}" OSIMADDLIB_LKIT)
267:         set(_INCLUDE_LIBNAME ${OSIMADDLIB_LKIT})
268:     else()
269:         set(_INCLUDE_LIBNAME ${OSIMADDLIB_KIT})
270:     endif()
271:     if(OSIMADDLIB_INCLUDEDIRS)
272:         foreach(dir ${OSIMADDLIB_INCLUDEDIRS})
273:             file(GLOB HEADERS ${dir}/*.h) # returns full pathnames
274:             if(OSIMADDLIB_INCLUDEINSTALLREL)
275:                 # Remove "INCLUDEINSTALLREL" from the installed location.
276:                 file(RELATIVE_PATH subdir
277:                     "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}${OSIMADDLIB_INCLUDEINSTALLREL}"
278:                     "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}${dir}")
279:             else()
280:                 set(subdir ${dir})
281:             endif()
282:             install(FILES ${HEADERS}
283:                 DESTINATION ${_INCLUDE_PREFIX}/${_INCLUDE_LIBNAME}/${subdir})
284:         endforeach(dir)
285:     else()
286:         install(FILES ${OSIMADDLIB_INCLUDES}
287:             DESTINATION ${_INCLUDE_PREFIX}/${_INCLUDE_LIBNAME})
288:     endif()
289: 
290:     # RPATH (so that libraries find library dependencies)
291:     # ---------------------------------------------------
292:     OpenSimAddInstallRPATHSelf(TARGET ${OSIMADDLIB_LIBRARY_NAME} LOADER)
293:     OpenSimAddInstallRPATHSimbody(TARGET ${OSIMADDLIB_LIBRARY_NAME} LOADER
294:         FROM "${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}")
295: 
296:     # Testing.
297:     # --------
298:     enable_testing()
299: 
300:     if(BUILD_TESTING)
301:         foreach(OSIMADDLIB_TESTDIR ${OSIMADDLIB_TESTDIRS})
302:             subdirs("${OSIMADDLIB_TESTDIR}")
303:         endforeach()
304:     endif()
305: 
306: endfunction()

308: # Copy a file from the directory containing test files (model files, data,
309: # etc.) to the directory in which a test will be executed. This function makes
310: # it easy to re-use files that are used in tests. With an easier mechanism for
311: # re-using these files, we won't end up version-controlling the same file in
312: # multiple test directories.
313: #
314: # Arguments are a list of files in the test resources directory
315: # (OPENSIM_SHARED_TEST_FILES_DIR) to copy.
316: function(OpenSimCopySharedTestFiles)
317:     if(BUILD_TESTING)
318:         foreach(filename ${ARGN})
319:             file(COPY "${OPENSIM_SHARED_TEST_FILES_DIR}/${filename}"
320:                  DESTINATION "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}")
321:         endforeach()
322:     endif()
323: endfunction()

325: # Create test targets for this directory.
326: # TESTPROGRAMS: Names of test CPP files. One test will be created for each cpp
327: #   of these files.
328: # DATAFILES: Files necessary to run the test. These will be copied into the
329: #   corresponding build directory.
330: # LINKLIBS: Arguments to TARGET_LINK_LIBRARIES.
331: # SOURCES: Extra source files for the executable.
332: #
333: # Here's an example:
334: #   file(GLOB TEST_PROGRAMS "test*.cpp")
335: #   file(GLOB DATA_FILES *.osim *.xml *.sto *.mot)
336: #   OpenSimAddTests(
337: #       TESTPROGRAMS ${TEST_PROGRAMS}
338: #       DATAFILES ${DATA_FILES}
339: #       LINKLIBS osimCommon osimSimulation osimAnalyses
340: #       )
341: function(OpenSimAddTests)
342: 
343:     if(BUILD_TESTING)
344: 
345:         # Parse arguments.
346:         # ----------------
347:         # http://www.cmake.org/cmake/help/v2.8.9/cmake.html#module:CMakeParseArguments
348:         set(options)
349:         set(oneValueArgs)
350:         set(multiValueArgs TESTPROGRAMS DATAFILES LINKLIBS SOURCES)
351:         cmake_parse_arguments(
352:             OSIMADDTESTS "${options}" "${oneValueArgs}" "${multiValueArgs}" ${ARGN})
353: 
354:         # If EXECUTABLE_OUTPUT_PATH is set, then that's where the tests will be
355:         # located. Otherwise, they are located in the current binary directory.
356:         if(EXECUTABLE_OUTPUT_PATH)
357:             set(TEST_PATH "${EXECUTABLE_OUTPUT_PATH}")
358:         else()
359:             set(TEST_PATH "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}")
360:         endif()
361: 
362:         # Make test targets.
363:         foreach(test_program ${OSIMADDTESTS_TESTPROGRAMS})
364:             # NAME_WE stands for "name without extension"
365:             get_filename_component(TEST_NAME ${test_program} NAME_WE)
366: 
367:             add_executable(${TEST_NAME} ${test_program}
368:                 ${OSIMADDTESTS_SOURCES})
369:             target_link_libraries(${TEST_NAME} ${OSIMADDTESTS_LINKLIBS})
370:             set(test_args "")
371:             if(APPLE)
372:                 list(APPEND test_args "~[win]~[linux]~[win/linux]~[linux/win]")
373:             endif()
374:             if(LINUX)
375:                 list(APPEND test_args "~[win]~[mac]~[win/mac]~[mac/win]")
376:             endif()
377:             if(WIN32)
378:                 list(APPEND test_args "~[mac]~[linux]~[mac/linux]~[linux/mac]~[unix]")
379:             endif()
380:             add_test(NAME ${TEST_NAME} COMMAND ${TEST_NAME} ${test_args})
381:             set_target_properties(${TEST_NAME} PROPERTIES
382:                 FOLDER "Tests"
383:             )
384:         endforeach()
385: 
386:         # Copy data files to build directory.
387:         foreach(data_file ${OSIMADDTESTS_DATAFILES})
388:             # This command re-copies the data files if they are modified;
389:             # custom commands don't do this.
390:             file(COPY "${data_file}" DESTINATION "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}")
391:         endforeach()
392: 
393:         #if(UNIX)
394:         #  add_definitions(-fprofile-arcs -ftest-coverage)
395:         #  link_libraries(gcov)
396:         #endif(UNIX)
397: 
398:     endif()
399: 
400: endfunction()

565: # Function to install shared libraries (any platform) from a dependency install
566: # directory into the OpenSim installation. One use case is to install libraries
567: # into the python package.
568: # PREFIX: A common part of the library file names (e.g., 'SimTK' or 'ezc3d').
569: #         This is to avoid copying unrelated files from a folder like /usr/lib.
570: # DEP_LIBS_DIR_WIN: Directory to search for the dependency's library, on
571: #         Windows.
572: # DEP_LIBS_DIR_UNIX: Directory to search for the dependency's library, on
573: #         UNIX (APPLE and Linux). Specify only the lib directory to avoid
574: #         searching all of /usr/local (if the dependency is installed to a
575: #         system location like this).
576: # OSIM_DESTINATION: Destination of the libraries within OpenSim's installation.
577: function(OpenSimInstallDependencyLibraries PREFIX DEP_LIBS_DIR_WIN
578:         DEP_LIBS_DIR_UNIX OSIM_DESTINATION)
579:     if(WIN32)
580:         file(GLOB_RECURSE LIBS "${DEP_LIBS_DIR_WIN}/${PREFIX}*.dll")
581:     else()
582:         if(APPLE)
583:             set(lib_ext "dylib")
584:         else()
585:             set(lib_ext "so*") # Trailing * for version #s.
586:         endif()
587:         file(GLOB_RECURSE LIBS "${DEP_LIBS_DIR_UNIX}/lib${PREFIX}*.${lib_ext}")
588:     endif()
589:     if(NOT LIBS)
590:         message(FATAL_ERROR "Zero shared libraries found in directory "
591:             "${DEP_INSTALL_DIR}.")
592:     endif()
593:     install(FILES ${LIBS} DESTINATION "${OSIM_DESTINATION}")
594: endfunction()

597: # Copy DLL files from a dependency's installation into the
598: # build and install directories. This is a Windows-specific function enabled
599: # only on Windows. The intention is to allow the runtime loader to find all 
600: # the required DLLs without editing the PATH environment variable.
601: # Arguments:
602: #   DEP_NAME: Name of the dependency (used to name a custom target)
603: #   DEP_BIN_DIR: The directory in the dependency containing DLLs to copy.

We need to extend the GitHub Actions CI workflow so that pull requests can optionally trigger an automated performance comparison between the PR's source branch and its target branch (e.g., `main`). 

    **Why:** We want a lightweight, opt-in way for reviewers and contributors to see whether a PR meaningfully changes runtime performance of core OpenSim simulations. The comparison should run on a dedicated performance-testing infrastructure, and the results should be posted back into the PR description as a markdown table.

    **How it should behave:**
    - Performance testing is triggered only when the literal string `[perf]` appears anywhere in the PR title *or* the PR body.
    - When triggered, the CI should:
      1. Build two macOS installer packages: one from the PR's target branch (the "base") and one from the PR's source branch.
      2. Upload both as build artifacts.
      3. Trigger a remote workflow in a separate repository (the performance harness) that downloads both artifacts, unzips them, runs a benchmark suite against each, and produces a `performance_results.md` table.
      4. Wait for the remote workflow to finish, download its result artifact, and post/overwrite the table in the PR description body using the GitHub API.
    - When not triggered, the CI should behave exactly as it does today (single Mac build job), except that the job name may appear as "skipped".

    **Additional requirements:**
    - Upgrade all `actions/upload-artifact` usages to `@v4` so that artifacts from individual jobs are available immediately (before the whole workflow finishes). This is already partially done on the Windows jobs; extend it to the Mac and Ubuntu jobs.
    - The Mac "source" job must preserve the existing build/install/test behavior, and pass its qualified version string (e.g., `4.1-2023-...`) as an output so the new comparison job knows what to download.
    - The new comparison job should use a shared personal access token (stored as a repository secret `PERF_DISPATCH_PAT`) to dispatch and await the remote workflow and to download cross-repo artifacts.

    The end-to-end flow is illustrated below (for a PR with `[perf]`):
    1. PR event triggers `continuous_integration.yml`.
    2. `Mac [target]` and `Mac [source]` both build and upload their install packages.
    3. A new job `performance_analysis` (dependent on both Mac jobs) sends a repository-dispatch event to the performance harness repo, passing the commit hash and artifact names.
    4. The same job waits for that remote workflow to complete.
    5. The remote workflow runs the benchmarks and uploads `performance_results.md`.
    6. The `performance_analysis` job downloads that file and updates the PR description body.

## Environment Setup
This is a GitHub Actions workflow change; no local install is needed to edit the file. To understand the existing CI structure, read `.github/workflows/continuous_integration.yml`. For the project's build/test conventions, refer to `CMakeLists.txt` (root) and the test `CMakeLists.txt` files under `OpenSim/*/Test`. For contributing guidelines see `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `DEVELOPING.md`.

arguments.newString:
mac_source:
    name: ${{ (contains(github.event.pull_request.title, '[perf]') || contains(github.event.pull_request.body, '[perf]')) && 'Mac [source]' || 'Mac' }}

    runs-on: macos-12

    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.configure.outputs.version }}

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - uses: actions/setup-python@v4
      with:
        python-version: '3.8'
        
    - name: Install Homebrew packages
      # Save the gfortran version to a file so we can use it in the cache key.
      run: |
        brew install cmake pkgconfig autoconf libtool automake wget pcre doxygen llvm
        brew reinstall gcc
        pip3 install numpy==1.20.2
        gfortran -v
        mkdir gfortran_version
        gfortran -v &> gfortran_version/gfortran_version.txt

    - name: Cache SWIG
      id: cache-swig
      uses: actions/cache@v3
      with:
        path: ~/swig
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-swig

    - name: Install SWIG
      # if: steps.cache-swig.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
      run: |
        mkdir ~/swig-source && cd ~/swig-source
        wget https://github.com/swig/swig/archive/refs/tags/v4.1.1.tar.gz
        tar xzf v4.1.1.tar.gz && cd swig-4.1.1
        sh autogen.sh && ./configure --prefix=$HOME/swig --disable-ccache
        make && make -j4 install

    - name: Cache dependencies
      id: cache-dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v3
      with:
        path: ~/opensim_dependencies_install
        # If Homebrew updates the gcc package, then our cache of IPOPT is invalid.
        # Specifically, the pkgcfg_lib_IPOPT_gfortran CMake variable becomes
        # undefined.
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-dependencies-${{ hashFiles('dependencies/*') }}-${{ hashFiles('gfortran_version/*') }}

    - name: Build dependencies
      if: steps.cache-dependencies.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
      run: |
        mkdir $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/../build_deps
        cd $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/../build_deps
        DEP_CMAKE_ARGS=($GITHUB_WORKSPACE/dependencies -LAH)
        DEP_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=~/opensim_dependencies_install)
        DEP_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release)
        DEP_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DSUPERBUILD_ezc3d=ON)
        DEP_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DOPENSIM_WITH_TROPTER=ON)
        DEP_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DOPENSIM_WITH_CASADI=ON)
        DEP_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DOPENSIM_DISABLE_LOG_FILE=ON)
        DEP_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11)
        printf '%s\n' "${DEP_CMAKE_ARGS[@]}"
        cmake "${DEP_CMAKE_ARGS[@]}"
        make --jobs 4

    - name: Configure opensim-core
      id: configure
      run: |
        mkdir $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/../build
        cd $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/../build
        OSIM_CMAKE_ARGS=($GITHUB_WORKSPACE -LAH)
        OSIM_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/../opensim-core-install)
        OSIM_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release)
        OSIM_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DOPENSIM_DEPENDENCIES_DIR=~/opensim_dependencies_install)
        OSIM_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11)
        OSIM_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DOPENSIM_C3D_PARSER=ezc3d)
        OSIM_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DBUILD_PYTHON_WRAPPING=on -DBUILD_JAVA_WRAPPING=on)
        OSIM_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DSWIG_EXECUTABLE=$HOME/swig/bin/swig)
        OSIM_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DOPENSIM_INSTALL_UNIX_FHS=OFF)
        OSIM_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DOPENSIM_DOXYGEN_USE_MATHJAX=off)
        # TODO: Update to simbody.github.io/latest
        OSIM_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DOPENSIM_SIMBODY_DOXYGEN_LOCATION="https://simbody.github.io/simtk.org/api_docs/simbody/latest/")
        OSIM_CMAKE_ARGS+=(-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-Werror, -Wdeprecated-copy")
        printf '%s\n' "${OSIM_CMAKE_ARGS[@]}"
        cmake "${OSIM_CMAKE_ARGS[@]}"
        VERSION=`cmake -L . | grep OPENSIM_QUALIFIED_VERSION | cut -d "=" -f2`
        echo $VERSION
        echo "VERSION=$VERSION" >> $GITHUB_ENV
        echo "version=$VERSION" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

    - name: Build opensim-core
      run: |
        cd $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/../build
        make --jobs 4

    - name: Test opensim-core
      run: |
        cd $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/../build
        ctest --parallel 4 --output-on-failure

    - name: Install opensim-core
      run: |
        cd $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/../build
        make doxygen
        make install
        cd $GITHUB_WORKSPACE
        mv $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/../opensim-core-install opensim-core-${{ steps.configure.outputs.version }}
        zip --symlinks --recurse-paths --quiet opensim-core-${{ steps.configure.outputs.version }}-11.zip opensim-core-${{ steps.configure.outputs.version }}
        mv opensim-core-${{ steps.configure.outputs.version }} $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/../opensim-core-install

    - name: Test Python bindings
      run: |
        cd $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/../opensim-core-install/sdk/Python
        # Run the python tests, verbosely.
        python3 -m unittest discover --start-directory opensim/tests --verbose

    - name: Upload opensim-core
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        # The upload-artifact zipping does not preserve symlinks or executable
        # bits. So we zip ourselves, even though this causes a double-zip.
        name: opensim-core-${{ steps.configure.outputs.version }}-mac
        path: opensim-core-${{ steps.configure.outputs.version }}-11.zip

391: /**
392:   This function tests numerically for continuity of a curve. The test is 
393:   performed by taking a point on the curve, and then two points (called the 
394:   shoulder points) to the left and right of the point in question. The value
395:   of the functions derivative is evaluated at each of the shoulder points and
396:   used to linearly extrapolate from the shoulder points back to the original 
397:   point. If the original point and the linear extrapolations of each of the 
398:   shoulder points agree within tol, then the curve is assumed to be 
399:   continuous.
400: 
401: 
402:   @param xV       Values to test for continuity, note that the first and last
403:   points cannot be tested
404: 
405:   @param yV       Function values at the test points
406: 
407:   @param dydxV    Function derivative values evaluated at xV
408: 
409:   @param d2ydx2V  Function 2nd derivative values (or estimates) evaluated at
410:   xV
411: 
412:   @param minTol   The minimum error allowed - this prevents the second order
413:   error term from going to zero
414: 
415:   @param taylorErrorMult  This scales the error tolerance. The default error
416:   tolerance is the 2nd-order Taylor series
417:   term.
418:   */
419: bool isFunctionContinuous(const SimTK::Vector& xV, const SimTK::Vector& yV,
420:         const SimTK::Vector& dydxV, const SimTK::Vector& d2ydx2V, 
421:         double minTol, double taylorErrorMult)
422: {
423:     bool flag_continuous = true;
424:     //double contErr = 0;
425: 
426:     double xL = 0;      // left shoulder point
427:     double xR = 0;      // right shoulder point
428:     double yL = 0;      // left shoulder point function value
429:     double yR = 0;      // right shoulder point function value
430:     double dydxL = 0;   // left shoulder point derivative value
431:     double dydxR = 0;   // right shoulder point derivative value
432: 
433:     double xVal = 0;    //x value to test
434:     double yVal = 0;    //Y(x) value to test
435: 
436:     double yValEL = 0;  //Extrapolation to yVal from the left
437:     double yValER = 0;  //Extrapolation to yVal from the right
438: 
439:     double errL = 0;
440:     double errR = 0;
441: 
442:     double errLMX = 0;
443:     double errRMX = 0;
444: 
445: 
446:     for(int i =1; i < xV.nelt()-1; i++){
447:         xVal = xV(i);
448:         yVal = yV(i);
449: 
450:         xL = xV(i-1);
451:         xR = xV(i+1);
452: 
453:         yL = yV(i-1);
454:         yR = yV(i+1);
455: 
456:         dydxL = dydxV(i-1);
457:         dydxR = dydxV(i+1);
458: 
459: 
460:         yValEL = yL + dydxL*(xVal-xL);
461:         yValER = yR - dydxR*(xR-xVal);
462: 
463:         errL = abs(yValEL-yVal);
464:         errR = abs(yValER-yVal);
465: 
466:         errLMX = abs(d2ydx2V(i-1)*0.5*(xVal-xL)*(xVal-xL));
467:         errRMX = abs(d2ydx2V(i+1)*0.5*(xR-xVal)*(xR-xVal));
468: 
469:         errLMX*=taylorErrorMult;
470:         errRMX*=taylorErrorMult;
471: 
472:         if(errLMX < minTol)
473:             errLMX = minTol;
474: 
475:         if(errRMX < minTol)
476:             errRMX = minTol; // to accommodate numerical
477:         //error in errL
478: 
479:         if(errL > errLMX || errR > errRMX){
480:             /*if(errL > errR){
481:               if(errL > contErr)
482:               contErr = errL;
483: 
484:               }else{
485:               if(errR > contErr)
486:               contErr = errR;
487:               }*/
488: 
489:             flag_continuous = false;
490:         }
491:     }
492: 
493:     return flag_continuous;//contErr;//
494: }

496: /**
497:   This function computes a standard central difference dy/dx. If 
498:   extrap_endpoints is set to 1, then the derivative at the end points is 
499:   estimated by linearly extrapolating the dy/dx values beside the end points
500: 
501:   @param x domain vector
502:   @param y range vector
503:   @param extrap_endpoints: (false)   Endpoints of the returned vector will be 
504:   zero, because a central difference
505:   is undefined at these endpoints
506:   (true)  Endpoints are computed by linearly 
507:   extrapolating using a first difference from 
508:   the neighboring 2 points
509:   @returns dy/dx computed using central differences
510:   */
511: SimTK::Vector calcCentralDifference(const SimTK::Vector& x, 
512:         const SimTK::Vector& y,                                          
513:         bool extrap_endpoints){
514: 
515: 
516:     SimTK::Vector dy(x.size());
517:     double dx1,dx2;
518:     double dy1,dy2;
519:     int size = x.size();
520:     for(int i=1; i<x.size()-1; i++){
521:         dx1 = x(i)-x(i-1);
522:         dx2 = x(i+1)-x(i);
523:         dy1 = y(i)-y(i-1);
524:         dy2 = y(i+1)-y(i);
525:         dy(i)= 0.5*dy1/dx1 + 0.5*dy2/dx2;
526:     }
527: 
528:     if(extrap_endpoints == true){
529:         dy1 = dy(2)-dy(1);
530:         dx1 = x(2)-x(1);
531:         dy(0) = dy(1) + (dy1/dx1)*(x(0)-x(1));
532: 
533:         dy2 = dy(size-2)-dy(size-3);
534:         dx2 = x(size-2)-x(size-3);
535:         dy(size-1) = dy(size-2) + (dy2/dx2)*(x(size-1)-x(size-2));
536:     }
537:     return dy;
538: }

568:   Class that makes a system so that SimTK's integrators (which require a system)
569:   can be used to numerically integrate the BezierCurveSet. This class is used

573:   A System is actually two classes: System::Guts does the work while System

576: class MySystemGuts : public SimTK::System::Guts {

582:     MySystemGuts* cloneImpl() const override {return new MySystemGuts(*this);}

585:     int realizeTopologyImpl(State& state) const override {

597:         //if(z>funcData.m_ic+SimTK::Eps)

603:             funcData.m_tmpXV(i) = funcData.m_splinedInput[i].
604:                 calcValue(SimTK::Vector(1,x));
605:         }
606: 
607:         //Update the dimension of the vector that we're integrating along
608:         funcData.m_tmpXV(funcData.m_intDim) = z;
609: 
610:         //Compute the function derivative at the location of interest
611:         Real dz = funcData.m_func.calcDerivative(funcData.m_tmpXV[0], funcData.m_tmpXV[1]);
612:         //if(z>funcData.m_ic+SimTK::Eps)
613:         //    printf(" dz: %f\n",dz);

623:             Vector&, SimTK::ProjectOptions) const {return 0;}

643: /**
644:   @param timeV A nx1 time vector to integrate along, which must monotonic 
645:   and increasing
646:   @param xM    A nxm matrix of row vectors, each corresponding to the row vector
647:   that should be applied to yF at time t
648:   @param yF    A function
649:   @param ic    The initial condition for the integral
650:   @param intAcc The accuracy of the integral
651:   @returns an nx2 matrix, time in column 0, integral of y in column 1
652:   */
653: SimTK::Matrix calcFunctionTimeIntegral( 
654:         const SimTK::Vector& timeV,
655:         const SimTK::Matrix& xM, 
656:         const MuscleFirstOrderActivationDynamicModel& yF,
657:         double ic, 
658:         int dim, 
659:         double startTime, 
660:         double endTime,
661:         double intAcc)
662: {
663:     SimTK::Matrix intXY(timeV.size(),2);
664: 
665:     //Populate FunctionData
666:     FunctionData fdata(yF);
667:     fdata.m_ic      = ic;
668:     fdata.m_intDim  = dim;
669:     fdata.m_tmpXV      = SimTK::Vector(xM.ncol());
670:     fdata.m_tmpXV = 0;
671: 
672:     SimTK::Array_< SimTK::Spline_<double> > splinedInput(xM.ncol());
673: 
674:     //Now spline xM over time
675:     for(int i=0; i<xM.ncol(); i++){        
676: 
677:         splinedInput[i] = SimTK::SplineFitter<Real>::
678:             fitForSmoothingParameter(1,timeV,xM(i),0).getSpline();
679:     }
680:     fdata.m_splinedInput = splinedInput;
681:     //FunctionData is now completely built
682: 
683: 
684:     //Set up system
685:     //double startTime = timeV(0);
686:     //double endTime   = timeV(timeV.nelt()-1);   
687:     MySystem sys(fdata);
688:     State initState = sys.realizeTopology();
689:     initState.setTime(startTime);
690: 
691: 
692:     RungeKuttaMersonIntegrator integ(sys);
693:     integ.setAccuracy(intAcc);
694:     integ.setFinalTime(endTime);
695:     integ.setReturnEveryInternalStep(false);
696:     integ.initialize(initState);
697: 
698:     int idx = 0;    
699:     double nextTimeInterval = 0;
700:     Integrator::SuccessfulStepStatus status;
701: 
702:     while (idx < timeV.nelt()) {      
703:         nextTimeInterval = timeV(idx);
704: 
705:         status=integ.stepTo(nextTimeInterval);
706: 
707:         // Use this for variable step output.
708:         //status = integ.stepTo(Infinity);
709: 
710:         if (status == Integrator::EndOfSimulation)
711:             break;
712: 
713:         const State& state = integ.getState();
714: 
715:         intXY(idx,0) = nextTimeInterval;
716:         intXY(idx,1) = (double)state.getZ()[0];                        
717: 
718:         idx++;
719: 
720:     }
721: 
722:     //cout << "Integrated Solution"<<endl;
723:     //cout << intXY << endl;
724: 
725: 
726:     //intXY.resizeKeep(idx,2);
727:     return intXY;
728: }

We need to add a new `StationDefinedFrame` component to OpenSim. This component is a `PhysicalFrame` whose position and orientation are automatically computed from `Station`s in the model, rather than being specified as a hard `(position, orientation)` tuple like `OffsetFrame`s.

The `StationDefinedFrame` component is defined by:
- Three non-co-located (triangular) points: `point_a`, `point_b`, `point_c`
- Two "registrations": `ab_axis` and `ab_x_ac_axis`, which map the computed vectors onto the resulting frame's axes
- An optional `origin_point` that defines the frame's origin (can be `point_a`, `point_b`, or `point_c`)

The mathematical formulation:
- `ab_axis = normalize(point_b - point_a)`
- `ab_x_ac_axis = normalize((point_b - point_a) x (point_c - point_a))`
- `third_axis = normalize((point_b - point_a) x ((point_b - point_a) x (point_c - point_a)))`
- These vectors are mapped to the frame's X, Y, Z axes based on the registration properties
- The resulting orientation matrix and position create a right-handed coordinate system

This is useful for more closely matching ISB's Grood-Suntay-style frame definitions, which are typically given in terms of fixed axes and cross products between points in space. It's intended to be used as an alternative to `OffsetFrame` for "landmark-driven" frame definition.

```cpp
template <class C>
SimTK::SpatialVec OffsetFrame<C>::
calcVelocityInGround(const SimTK::State& state) const
{
    // The rigid offset of the OffsetFrame expressed in ground
    const SimTK::Vec3& r = this->getParentFrame().getTransformInGround(state).R()*
        getOffsetTransform().p();
    // Velocity of the base frame in ground
    SimTK::SpatialVec V_GF = this->getParentFrame().getVelocityInGround(state);
    // translational velocity needs additional omega x r term due to offset 
    V_GF(1) += V_GF(0) % r;

    return V_GF;
}

template <class C>
SimTK::SpatialVec OffsetFrame<C>::
calcAccelerationInGround(const SimTK::State& state) const
{
    // The rigid offset of the OffsetFrame expressed in ground
    const SimTK::Vec3& r = this->getParentFrame().getTransformInGround(state).R()*
        getOffsetTransform().p();
    // Velocity of the parent frame in ground
    const SimTK::SpatialVec& V_GF = this->getParentFrame().getVelocityInGround(state);
    // Velocity of the parent frame in ground
    SimTK::SpatialVec A_GF = getParentFrame().getAccelerationInGround(state);
    A_GF[1] += (A_GF[0] % r + V_GF[0] % (V_GF[0] % r));

    return A_GF;
}
```

## 6. How Frame declares sockets / the BaseFrame pattern

### `Frame` itself declares NO socket to a base frame
There is no `base_frame` or `parent` socket on `Frame` in this codebase. The base-frame relation is computed, not connected:
- `Frame::findBaseFrame()` → virtual `extendFindBaseFrame()` → `PhysicalFrame` returns `*this`; `OffsetFrame` delegates to parent `findBaseFrame()`.
- `Frame::findTransformInBaseFrame()` → virtual `extendFindTransformInBaseFrame()` → `PhysicalFrame` returns identity; `OffsetFrame` chains `parent.findTransformInBaseFrame() * getOffsetTransform()`.

### Socket declaration macros — `/code/OpenSim/Common/ComponentSocket.h`
The single-value socket macro, `OpenSim_DECLARE_SOCKET(cname, T, comment)` (lines 998-1026), expands (essentially) to:
```cpp
OpenSim::PropertyIndex PropertyIndex_socket_##cname {
    this->template constructSocket<T>(#cname,
            "Path to a Component that satisfies the Socket '"
            #cname "' of type " #T " (description: " comment ").")
};
void connectSocket_##cname(const OpenSim::Object& object) {
    this->updSocket(#cname).connect(object);
}
```
So declaring `OpenSim_DECLARE_SOCKET(parent, PhysicalFrame, "...")` in `OffsetFrame.h:78` creates:
- a socket named **`parent`** of type **`PhysicalFrame`**, backed by a `socket_parent` property, and
- a convenience `connectSocket_parent(obj)`.

There is also a forward-declared variant, `OpenSim_DECLARE_SOCKET_FD` (ComponentSocket.h:1077-1106) used when the connectee type can only be forward declared (e.g. `Geometry`'s `frame` socket). Its companion definition macro:
```cpp
#define OpenSim_DEFINE_SOCKET_FD(cname, Class)                              \
OpenSim::PropertyIndex Class::constructSocket_##cname() {                   \
    using T = _socket_##cname##_type;                                       \
    std::string typeStr = T::getClassName();                                \
    return this->template constructSocket<T>(#cname,                        \
        "Path to a Component that satisfies the Socket '"                   \
        #cname "' of type " + typeStr + ".");                               \
}
```
used by `Geometry` at `/code/OpenSim/Simulation/Model/Geometry.cpp:38`:
```cpp
OpenSim_DEFINE_SOCKET_FD(frame, Geometry);
```
with the declaration in `/code/OpenSim/Simulation/Model/Geometry.h:68-70`:
```cpp
    OpenSim_DECLARE_SOCKET_FD(frame, Frame,
        "The frame to which this geometry is attached. Note, being connected "
        "to a Frame means its transform is used to position this Geometry." );
```

### `Component::constructSocket` — `/code/OpenSim/Common/Component.h:2711-2730`
```cpp
    template <typename T>
    PropertyIndex constructSocket(const std::string& name,
                                     const std::string& propertyComment) {
        OPENSIM_THROW_IF(_socketsTable.count(name), Exception,
            getConcreteClassName() + " already has a socket named '"
            + name + "'.");

        // ...
        PropertyIndex propIndex = this->template addProperty<std::string>(
                "socket_" + name , propertyComment, "");
        // We must create the Property first: the Socket needs the property's
        // index in order to access the property later on.

            new Socket<T>(name, propIndex, SimTK::Stage::Topology, *this));
```

So the **XML element for setting a socket path is `socket_<name>`** (e.g. `socket_parent` for OffsetFrame, `socket_parent_frame` for Station, `socket_frame` for Geometry). The backing property is a single-value `Property<std::string>`.

### About "addInlinedSocket"
It does not exist. Socket creation is *only* through the macros → `constructSocket`. (Do not confuse with `attachGeometry(...)` / subcomponent adoption, which call `prependComponentPathToConnecteePath`.)

### List sockets
There is no `OpenSim_DECLARE_LIST_SOCKET` in this version (the only such macro is in the sandbox `/code/OpenSim/Sandbox/ListInput.h:19-21`, which is not production code). `AbstractSocket` *does* support a list mode: `_isList(getConnecteePathProp().isListProperty())` (`ComponentSocket.h:264`), i.e. if the backing `socket_<name>` property is a list property. However the production `Socket<T>` holds a single connectee (`ComponentSocket.h:368,440-444`), so for a `StationDefinedFrame` that owns multiple stations you should rely on an **owning list property of Station subcomponents** (like `GeometryPath`'s `PathPointSet`, `/code/OpenSim/Simulation/Model/GeometryPath.h:64-65`), not a list socket.

# Frame Ordering in OpenSim's Model during System Construction

## Executive summary

In this version of OpenSim (master, commit `ed146ec`), **frame ordering is done in `Model::extendConnectToModel(Model&)`**, NOT in `extendFinalizeFromProperties`, and **there is no `_frames` member, `orderFrames` method, or `SerialList<Frame>`**. The old `FrameSet` was removed from `Model`. Ordering is achieved by walking the `parent` socket dependency chain of `PhysicalOffsetFrame`s and appending them to the `Component::_orderedSubcomponents` list via `setNextSubcomponentInSystem()`. Ground and Body frames are ordered by SimTK's `MultibodyGraphMaker` (the multibody tree), while offset frames are ordered by a hand-written dependency-chain walk (the code you want to replace with a topological sort).

---

```cpp
966:        std::vector<const PhysicalOffsetFrame*> parentPofs;
967:        while (parentPof) {
```

**How test source files map to executables.** Tests are discovered by the glob `test*.cpp`; each file's basename becomes the executable and CTest test name. This is implemented in `cmake/OpenSimMacros.cmake` in the `OpenSimAddTests` function (lines 341–400):

```cmake
function(OpenSimAddTests)
    ...
    set(multiValueArgs TESTPROGRAMS DATAFILES LINKLIBS SOURCES)
    cmake_parse_arguments(
        OSIMADDTESTS "${options}" "${oneValueArgs}" "${multiValueArgs}" ${ARGN})
    ...
    foreach(test_program ${OSIMADDTESTS_TESTPROGRAMS})
        # NAME_WE stands for "name without extension"
        get_filename_component(TEST_NAME ${test_program} NAME_WE)

        add_executable(${TEST_NAME} ${test_program}
            ${OSIMADDTESTS_SOURCES})
        target_link_libraries(${TEST_NAME} ${OSIMADDTESTS_LINKLIBS})
        set(test_args "")
        ...
        add_test(NAME ${TEST_NAME} COMMAND ${TEST_NAME} ${test_args})
        set_target_properties(${TEST_NAME} PROPERTIES
            FOLDER "Tests")
    endforeach()
    ...
endfunction()
```

So `testFrames.cpp` → executable/test `testFrames`; `testJoints.cpp` → `testJoints`. **There is no `testWeldJoint.cpp` in this repo anymore** (joint tests are consolidated in `OpenSim/Simulation/SimbodyEngine/Test/testJoints.cpp`). The joint test directory uses the identical pattern (`OpenSim/Simulation/SimbodyEngine/Test/CMakeLists.txt`, lines 1–9):

```cmake
file(GLOB TEST_PROGS "test*.cpp")
file(GLOB TEST_FILES *.osim *.xml *.sto *.mot)

OpenSimAddTests(
    TESTPROGRAMS ${TEST_PROGS}
    DATAFILES ${TEST_FILES}
    LINKLIBS osimSimulation osimCommon osimAnalyses
    )
```

Consequence: to add a new test like `testStationDefinedFrame.cpp`, you only need to drop the file into the directory — the glob picks it up unconditionally (no per-test editing needed). To add a new `.osim` data file it is also auto-globbed via `TEST_FILES`.

**Not present anywhere under `OpenSim/Simulation/Model`** (grep returns zero matches in that directory). The only production usages in C++ are in `OpenSim/Simulation/OpenSense/`:

**Construction** — `OpenSim/Simulation/OpenSense/IMUPlacer.cpp` lines 116–128:

```cpp
116:        SimTK::CoordinateDirection directionOnIMU(SimTK::ZAxis);
117:        int direction = 1;
118:        if (imu_axis.front() == '-') direction = -1;
119:        char& back = imu_axis.back();
120:        if (back == 'x')
121:            directionOnIMU =
122:                    SimTK::CoordinateDirection(SimTK::XAxis, direction);
123:        else if (back == 'y')
124:            directionOnIMU =
125:                    SimTK::CoordinateDirection(SimTK::YAxis, direction);
126:        else if (back == 'z')
127:            directionOnIMU =
128:                    SimTK::CoordinateDirection(SimTK::ZAxis, direction);
```

**Reading** — `OpenSim/Simulation/OpenSense/OpenSenseUtilities.cpp` lines 209–233: it is taken as a `const SimTK::CoordinateDirection` parameter, then read with `.getAxis()` and `.getDirection()`:

```cpp
209:            const SimTK::CoordinateDirection baseHeadingDirection)
...
231:        UnitVec3 baseSegmentXHeading = base_R(baseHeadingDirection.getAxis());
232:        if (baseHeadingDirection.getDirection() < 0)
233:            baseSegmentXHeading = baseSegmentXHeading.negate();
```

So the **exact API calls are `.getAxis()` (returns `SimTK::CoordinateAxis`) and `.getDirection()` (returns `int`, always `1` or `-1`)**. There is no `.getAxisOrDirectionCoords()` or `.getPropertyName()` — the type is a plain SimTK class, not an OpenSim property-accessor.

**Full SimTK `CoordinateDirection` API** (the SimTK headers are a build dependency; the in-repo mirror that documents the API is `Bindings/SWIGSimTK/CoordinateAxis.h`, class at lines 244–334):
- ctors: `CoordinateDirection(const CoordinateAxis& axis)` (line 252, implicit, positive); `CoordinateDirection(const CoordinateAxis& axis, Negative)` (line 257); `CoordinateDirection(const CoordinateAxis& axis, int direction)` (line 267, runtime direction ±1)
- `CoordinateAxis getAxis() const` (line 274)
- `int getDirection() const` (line 277)
- `bool hasSameAxis(const CoordinateDirection&) const` (281), `bool isSameAxisAndDirection(const CoordinateDirection&) const` (287)
- `int dotProduct(const CoordinateDirection&) const` (293), `int crossProductSign(...)` (302), `CoordinateAxis crossProductAxis(...)` (314), `CoordinateAxis crossProduct(const CoordinateDirection&, int& sign)` (324)
- Global constants: `XAxis, YAxis, ZAxis` (positive `CoordinateDirection`s), `NegXAxis, NegYAxis, NegZAxis` (lines 350–355)
- operator overloads: `-XAxis → NegXAxis`, `-CoordAxis → negative dir`, `-CoordinateDirection → opposite` (lines 367–409)

To use it in a C++ file, include a SimTK header (e.g., `<SimTKcommon/Scalar.h>` or more simply `<Simbody.h>` / any OpenSim header already pulling SimTK in, since OpenSim builds on SimTK).
