## 8. `Model.cpp` `extendFinalizeFromProperties` and how `PhysicalFrame`s are ordered

`Model::extendFinalizeFromProperties` is at `OpenSim/Simulation/Model/Model.cpp` lines 710–732:

```cpp
710: void Model::extendFinalizeFromProperties()
711: {
712:     Super::extendFinalizeFromProperties();
713:
714:     // wipe-out the existing System
715:     _matter.reset();
716:     _forceSubsystem.reset();
717:     _contactSubsystem.reset();
718:     _system.reset();
719:
720:     if(getForceSet().getSize()>0)
721:     {
722:         ForceSet &fs = updForceSet();
723:         // Update internal subsets of the ForceSet
724:         fs.updActuators();
725:         fs.updMuscles();
726:     }
727:
728:     std::string warn = getWarningMesssageForMotionTypeInconsistency();
729:     appendToValidationLog(warn);
730:
731:     updCoordinateSet().populate(*this);
732: }
```

It does **not** order PhysicalFrames — ordering happens later in `Model::extendConnectToModel` (line 812), which builds a multibody tree and assigns System order:

- Lines 827–831: `createMultibodyTree();` then `_multibodyTree.generateGraph();`.
- Lines 835–837: **Ground is first**: `setNextSubcomponentInSystem(ground)`.
- Lines 851–913: mobilizers (joints/bodies) are ordered per the tree (`setNextSubcomponentInSystem(*joint)` line 909).
- Lines 951–983 — the key `PhysicalOffsetFrame` ordering block:

```cpp
951:     // Now include all remaining Components beginning with PhysicalOffsetFrames
952:     // since Constraints, Forces and other components can only be applied to
953:     // PhyicalFrames, which include PhysicalOffsetFrames.
954:     // PhysicalOffsetFrames require that their parent frame (a PhysicalFrame)
955:     // be added to the System first. So for each PhysicalOffsetFrame locate its
956:     // parent and verify its presence in the _orderedList otherwise add it first.
957:     auto poFrames = updComponentList<PhysicalOffsetFrame>();
958:     for (auto& pof : poFrames) {
963:         pof.finalizeConnections(*this);
964:         const PhysicalOffsetFrame* parentPof =
965:             dynamic_cast<const PhysicalOffsetFrame*>(&pof.getParentFrame());
966:         std::vector<const PhysicalOffsetFrame*> parentPofs;
967:         while (parentPof) {
968:             const auto found =
969:                 std::find(parentPofs.begin(), parentPofs.end(), parentPof);
970:             OPENSIM_THROW_IF_FRMOBJ(found != parentPofs.end(),
971:                 PhysicalOffsetFramesFormLoop, (*found)->getName());
972:             parentPofs.push_back(parentPof);
973:             // Given a chain of offsets, the most proximal must have Ground or
974:             // Body as its parent. When that happens we can stop.
975:             parentPof =
976:                 dynamic_cast<const PhysicalOffsetFrame*>(&parentPof->getParentFrame());
977:         }
978:         while (parentPofs.size()) {
979:             setNextSubcomponentInSystem(*parentPofs.back());
980:             parentPofs.pop_back();
981:         }
982:         setNextSubcomponentInSystem(pof);
983:     }
984:
985:     // and everything else including Forces, Controllers, etc...
987:     auto components = getImmediateSubcomponents();
988:     for (const auto& comp : components) {
989:         setNextSubcomponentInSystem(comp.getRef());
990:     }
```

Per-frame finalize: `PhysicalFrame::extendFinalizeFromProperties` (`PhysicalFrame.cpp` lines 55–58) just calls `Super` (Frame/Component). `OffsetFrame<C>::extendFinalizeFromProperties` (`OffsetFrame.h` lines 349–355) computes the cached offset transform:

```cpp
350: void OffsetFrame<C>::extendFinalizeFromProperties()
351: {
352:     Super::extendFinalizeFromProperties();
353:     _offsetTransform.updP() = get_translation();
354:     _offsetTransform.updR().setRotationToBodyFixedXYZ(get_orientation());
355: }
```

Cross-check note for the other agent: a new `StationDefinedFrame` (deriving from `PhysicalFrame`, like `PhysicalOffsetFrame`) will be picked up automatically by `updComponentList<PhysicalOffsetFrame>()` in this block **only if it derives from `PhysicalOffsetFrame`**. If it derives directly from `PhysicalFrame`, it is NOT in the special ordering block and would fall into the generic "everything else" loop at lines 987–990 — which would break the *parent-before-child* guarantee for a frame referenced as a Joint socket. To behave correctly, it must either derive from `PhysicalOffsetFrame` (or `Station`-aggregating physical offset frame) or the user must add its ordering in this block. Also note `Frame::extendFinalizeFromProperties`/`ModelComponentSet.h` style (line 65-66 in that header) call `Super::extendFinalizeFromProperties()` first in each layer.

## 9. How a `Station` is serialized in an .osim file

**There is no `<Station>` block anywhere in the repo's .osim/.xml files** (searched the whole repo). Station's declaration (`OpenSim/Simulation/Model/Station.h`, lines 42–51):

```cpp
42: class OSIMSIMULATION_API Station : public Point {
43: OpenSim_DECLARE_CONCRETE_OBJECT(Station, Point);
44: public:
48:     OpenSim_DECLARE_PROPERTY(location, SimTK::Vec3,
49:         "The fixed location of the station expressed in its parent frame.");
50:     OpenSim_DECLARE_SOCKET(parent_frame, PhysicalFrame,
51:         "The frame to which this station is fixed.");
```

Construction (`Station.cpp` lines 86–92):

```cpp
86: void Station::constructProperties()
87: {
88:     //Default location
89:     SimTK::Vec3 origin(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
90:     // Location in Body
91:     constructProperty_location(origin);
92: }
```

So a 4.x `Station` serializes with a **`<location>` property** (not `location_in_parent`) and a **`parent_frame` socket** (serialized as `<socket_parent_frame>` in 4.x files; see the joint example at BouncingBall... line 50). The `<location_in_parent>` element belongs to **Joint**/`PhysicalOffsetFrame`/wrap-point contexts, NOT to `Station` — e.g. `double_pendulum.osim` line 166 (`<location_in_parent>0 0 0</location_in_parent>` inside `PinJoint`) and many wrap-object examples.

The closest existing serialized example is a **`<Marker>`**, which is a subclass of `Station` (`Marker.h` line 44: `OpenSim_DECLARE_CONCRETE_OBJECT(Marker, Station);`). Full Marker examples are in `OpenSim/Simulation/Test/testMomentArmsConstraintA.osim` lines 6616–6623 (3.x-era format using `<body>` instead of a socket):

```xml
6616: 				<Marker name="asis_r">
6617: 					<!--Body segment in the model on which the marker resides.-->
6618: 					<body>pelvis</body>
6619: 					<!--Location of a marker on the body segment.-->
6620: 					<location> 0.014 0 0.128</location>
6621: 					<!--Flag (true or false) specifying whether or not a marker should be kept fixed in the marker placement step.  i.e. If false, the marker is allowed to move.-->
6622: 					<fixed>false</fixed>
6623: 				</Marker>
```

Simpler version at `OpenSim/Simulation/Test/arm26.osim` lines 1273–1282:

```xml
1273: 				<Marker name="r_acromion">
1275: 					<body> ground </body>
1277: 					<location>      -0.01256000       0.04000000       0.17000000 </location>
1281: 					<fixed> false </fixed>
```

For the modern 4.x format with explicit sockets, a `Marker`/`Station` element would instead use `<socket_parent_frame>...</socket_parent_frame>` and `<location>`, analogous to how `Point`-based components' sockets serialize (see `socket_parent_frame` in `BouncingBall_SmoothSphereHalfSpace.osim` line 50). A matching `StationDefinedFrame` example model would therefore contain, e.g.:

```xml
<FrameSet>
    <objects>
        <StationDefinedFrame name="...">
            <socket_parent>...path to parent PhysicalFrame...</socket_parent>
            <translation>0 0 0</translation>     <!-- if derived from OffsetFrame -->
            <orientation>0 0 0</orientation>
            <axis>...coordinate direction...</axis>   <!-- new property -->
            <socket_location>...station/path...</socket_location>   <!-- new socket -->
        </StationDefinedFrame>
    </objects>
</FrameSet>
```

(Element names will depend on the final `OpenSim_DECLARE_PROPERTY`/`OpenSim_DECLARE_SOCKET` names you choose; the existing `PhysicalOffsetFrame` block in `BouncingBall_SmoothSphereHalfSpace.osim` lines 140–158 is the exact structural template to copy.)

The `StationDefinedFrame` component implementation is complete. Summary of the work:

## New files
- **`OpenSim/Simulation/Model/StationDefinedFrame.h`** — `PhysicalFrame` subclass with `ab_axis`/`ab_x_ac_axis` properties (`SimTK::CoordinateDirection`), sockets for `point_a`/`point_b`/`point_c`/`origin_point` (all `Station`), constructors, accessors, and full documentation of the math, serialization format (`+X`, `-Y`, `Z`, …), and known limitations (shared base frame, chaining, joint-child restrictions).
- **`OpenSim/Simulation/Model/StationDefinedFrame.cpp`** — implements `normalize(b−a)` and `normalize((b−a)×(c−a))` mapped onto the registered axes, third axis chosen for a right-handed system; validation for co-located/collinear points, same-axis registrations, and differing base frames; `extendAddToSystem` reuses the shared base's `MobilizedBodyIndex`; velocity/acceleration treat the frame as rigid in its base.
- **`OpenSim/Simulation/Test/testStationDefinedFrame.cpp`** — Catch2 tests: known-value transforms (identity and non-identity frames, origin default vs explicit), frame on a rotated body, serialization round-trip, frame as a joint (`WeldJoint`) parent, degenerate-config error cases, and loading the example model.
- **`OpenSim/Simulation/Test/BasicModelWithStationDefinedFrame.osim`** — block body welded to ground with four `Station`s and a `StationDefinedFrame` (`ab_axis`=+X, `ab_x_ac_axis`=+Z, identity in ground).

## Modified files
- **`OpenSim/Common/Property.h` / `Property.cpp`** — added `Property<SimTK::CoordinateDirection>::TypeHelper` and custom stream serialization (`+X`/`-Y`/`Z` format) so the properties work in `.osim` files (this type previously had no property support).
- **`OpenSim/Simulation/Model/Model.cpp`** — replaced the `PhysicalOffsetFrame`-only ordering walk with a Kahn topological sort over all dependent `Frame`s (offset + station-defined), preserving the `PhysicalOffsetFramesFormLoop` exception for cycles.
- **`RegisterTypes_osimSimulation.cpp`** / **`osimSimulation.h`** — register `StationDefinedFrame` and add its include to the umbrella header.
- **`OpenSim/Tests/Components/testComponents.cpp`** — skip `StationDefinedFrame` in the generic framework test (transitive `Station` sockets).
- **`CHANGELOG.md`** — entry under v4.5.

No build environment exists to compile, so correctness rests on the inspection/consistency checks performed: brace balance, XML well-formedness, no C++20 features, confirmed API signatures against the codebase, and all previously-accepted files left untouched.

Note for the PR: consumers building the Python/Java bindings will additionally need `StationDefinedFrame` added to the SWIG `.i` interface, which is outside the C++ test scope here.
